name: Frumentius
otherNames: Abba Salama, "the Father of Peace" (in the Ethiopian tradition, by Hartranft and the Dictionary of Christian Biography)
knownFor: A shipwrecked Roman captive who brought Christianity to the kingdom of Axum and was made its first bishop by Athanasius of Alexandria.
dates: Fourth century; the date of his consecration is disputed (see What is uncertain)
place: Axum (Auxumis), in the kingdom of Aksum, in what is now Ethiopia
role: Captive, royal official, missionary and first bishop of Axum

traces: The church of Axum, which Rufinus of Aquileia says he began among the Roman merchants and the king's household, and over which Athanasius of Alexandria made him bishop.
remembered: The Ethiopian tradition, Hartranft says, calls him the Abba Salama of Axum.
The emperor Constantius tried to have him replaced by an Arian bishop, Theophilus, which Blomfield Jackson notes from Athanasius's Apology to Constantius 31; the attempt did not succeed.

uncertain: Rufinus says he had the whole account from Edesius, Frumentius's companion, after Edesius became a presbyter at Tyre. So the story of his early life rests on that one chain. Socrates of Constantinople and Sozomen retell Rufinus, and Valesius, in A. C. Zenos's edition, says Socrates copied him almost word for word.

When he was consecrated is disputed. Rufinus places it soon after Athanasius became bishop, about 328. Valesius put it later, under Constantius, and Archibald Robertson, who edited Athanasius in English, agrees, since the dates in the story and the emperor's letter fit a later year.
The year of his death is not given in any held source.
"India" in these writers means Ethiopia, Zenos notes; the kingdom is Aksum, with its city of Axum.
